Class SymbolList<S extends Symbol>

java.lang.Object
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.StoryGraphCollection<S>
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.StoryGraphList<S>
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.SymbolList<S>
Type Parameters:
S - the type of symbol in this collection
All Implemented Interfaces:
Iterable<S>, RandomAccess
Direct Known Subclasses:
ActionList, CharacterList, FluentList, ValueList
public abstract class SymbolList<S extends Symbol> extends StoryGraphList<S>
A collection of symbols of the same type. A symbol can be accessed by its ID number or name.
Author:
Stephen G. Ware

    • add

      public abstract S add(String name)
      Creates a new symbol of this type with the given name, or returns the existing symbol with that name if one already exists. If a new symbol is created, its ID number will be the next in the sequence (i.e. the size of this collection at the time the symbol is created).

      This method updates the story graph's meta-data with the new number of symbols of this type. It also updates the last modified timestamp.

      Parameters:
      name - the name of the symbol to create or find
      Returns:
      a new symbol with that given name, or the existing symbol with that name if one already exists

    • add

      protected void add(S symbol)
      Adds a new symbol to this collection. This method expects the ID number of the symbol to be the size of the collection; in other words, adding the new symbol to the end of the list of symbols should add the symbol at the index that matches its ID number.

      This method updates the story graph's meta-data with the new number of symbols of this type. It also updates the last modified timestamp.

      Parameters:
      symbol - the new symbol to be added to the collection

    • sort

      public boolean sort(Comparator<? super S> comparator, Status status)
      Sorts and renumbers the symbols of this collection based on the given comparator. If the order of any symbols changes, their ID numbers will be reassigned to be sequential.

      If this method modifies the order of elements, it updates the story graph's meta-data last modified timestamp.

      Parameters:
      comparator - the comparator that defines the new order of elements
      status - a status object that will be updated while this method runs to reflect its current progress
      Returns:
      true if any elements were reordered, false if all elements remained in the same order

    • sort

    • prune

      protected boolean prune(Predicate<Object> predicate, Status status)
      Description copied from class: StoryGraphCollection
      For each element in this collection, this method removes any reference in that element to other elements whose ID numbers have been set to Settings.PRUNED and, if the given predicate returns true, sets the element's ID number to Settings.PRUNED to signal that it should also be removed from this graph. This method does not remove elements from this collection for which the predicate returns true; it only sets their ID numbers to signal that they should later be removed, which typically happens when the collection is renumbered.
      Specified by:
      prune in class StoryGraphCollection<S extends Symbol>
      Parameters:
      predicate - a predicate that specifies which elements should be removed from from a story graph
      status - a status object that will be updated while this method runs to reflect its current progress
      Returns:
      true if the predicate returned true for any elements in this collection

      Description copied from class: StoryGraphList
